estimand_functional: \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)=\{T\subseteq\mathcal V:|T|=r,\ \exists t\text{ ordering }T\text{ with }\bar Q_{tt}\succ0\text{ and }L_t^{-1}P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T}L_t^{-\mathsf T}\text{ diagonal and nonnegative for every }e\}\), where \(\bar Q=\sum_{e=1}^E\Delta_e\) and \(L_t\) is the unit-lower factor in the positive \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factorization of \(\bar Q_{tt}\).

sampling_model.design: Independent multi-sample Gaussian covariance experiment across environments \(e\in\mathcal E\) for inference; the population necessity argument itself uses only the declared second-moment invariance and independence conditions.
sampling_model.units: For each environment, \(n_e\) independent centered observations \(Y_{ei}\in\mathbb R^d\).
sampling_model.treatment: Unknown soft interventions change exactly \(r\) observed structural-noise variances.  The baseline is a minimum-variance condition, shifts are nonnegative, and each target changes in at least one nonbaseline environment; no common calibration environment is required.
sampling_model.overlap: Covariances obey \(mI_d\preceq\Sigma_e\preceq MI_d\); no separation from covariance-profile collisions is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The empirical covariance tuple is used directly.  Stationary latent confounding and stationary measurement error cancel from population covariance differences, and the aggregate of those differences carries the changing subspace.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 characterizes the LIT output under latent confounding as a candidate superset of the observed intervention targets.

Theorem 1 gives uniqueness of a global joint diagonalizer under profile noncollinearity in a model that permits cyclic structural coefficients; it does not impose the present acyclic labeling constraint, target coverage, or an exact-rank designated carrier.

The identifiability theorem recovers an unmixing matrix up to scaling and permutation under variation and noncollinearity conditions; aggregate exact rank and aggregate shift-range inclusion here are consequences or explicit premises of a different acyclic target-fiber model, not cited coroICA assumptions.

The paper develops sign-and-permutation, distinct-eigenvalue, eigen-decomposition, and restricted rotation-set results for heteroskedastic structural VARs, not a complete family of labeled acyclic covariance-shift targets.
Theorem 1 constructs a test-inversion confidence set for a causal effect while retaining uncertainty over two linear causal structures.
The paper constructs random sets with pointwise and uniform asymptotic coverage for an identified set and its images by objective-function inversion.

Theorems 1--2 give weak-identification-robust chi-square inference for full and selected structural parameters in heteroskedastic models, not a geometry-free power envelope for a discrete target fiber.

tldr: Under a designed minimum-variance baseline, stationary latent confounding and measurement error cancel from covariance differences.  No common all-target reference is needed: the aggregate carrier \(\bar Q=\sum_{e=1}^E\Delta_e\) has rank \(r\) and contains every shift range whenever shifts are nonnegative and every target changes in at least one environment.  A size-\(r\) label set is compatible exactly when some ordering passes the aggregate principal-block \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) certificate, and every certificate has an acyclic Gaussian realization at any positive-definite baseline with strictly positive structural and measurement noises.  Subset-memoized pivots compute the complete family, while feasible-point augmentation gives always-nonempty honest family regions.  Information distance separates consistency from bounded-information impossibility, but local optimal certification is indexed by the full tangent-cone geometry rather than by distance alone.

project_justification.gap: Unknown-target methods with latent confounding return candidate supersets, whereas covariance-difference methods recover a global mixing matrix only under profile separation.  Existing heteroskedastic diagonalization and rotation-set results do not characterize every labeled acyclic target set at profile collisions or lift each certificate to a positive-noise SCM.
project_justification.niche: A minimum-variance baseline, nonnegative shifts, and panel-wide target coverage make the aggregate covariance difference a rank-\(r\) carrier.  Acyclicity then supplies a triangular labeling constraint that can be checked on candidate principal blocks even when no individual environment changes every target and individual changed columns are not globally identified.
project_justification.fill: The project gives an aggregate-carrier if-and-only-if labeled-fiber theorem, an arbitrary-baseline positive-noise converse, a signed-shift boundary witness, a complete subset recursion, always-nonempty honest family inference, a quantitative four-node collision, and a geometry-indexed characterization showing why no universal local envelope can depend only on scalar information distance.

related_work: Yang, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash motivate unknown-target matching under latent confounding but characterize a candidate superset rather than the complete labeled fiber.  BACKSHIFT motivates covariance differencing and global diagonalization, but it permits cyclic structural coefficients and does not assume a common all-target reference or a designated exact-rank carrier; the present acyclic aggregate-carrier theorem is therefore a different result.  coroICA likewise motivates differencing away group-wise stationary noise and uses variation conditions for unmixing recovery; aggregate exact rank and aggregate range inclusion here are derived consequences of nonnegative covered shifts in the legal causal model, or explicit premises for standalone observed-tuple reconstruction, rather than attributed coroICA hypotheses.  Yang et al. analyze measurement error after a recoverable mixing matrix is available, whereas invariant positive measurement error here cancels before the target fiber is characterized.  Bacchiocchi et al. study sign/permutation equivalence, distinct heteroskedastic eigenvalues, and restricted rotation sets at multiplicity, not the complete discrete family of observed acyclic target labels.  Jaber et al. and Squires et al. make completeness over unknown-target equivalence classes algorithmically central under graphical oracle conditions; the present recursion uses exact aggregate covariance pivots.  Brown--Purves selection and Romano--Shaikh identified-set inversion motivate the inference construction, while Lewis motivates robust inference near weak heteroskedastic separation.  Perturb-seq and Sci-Plex supply an application domain, but the output here concerns effective structural-noise targets only when the narrower covariance model is scientifically defensible.
technical_internal_limitation: The model assumes environment-invariant structural coefficients, latent covariance, and measurement-error covariance, fixed dimension, a minimum-variance baseline, nonnegative structural-variance increments, and panel-wide coverage of every declared target.  For arbitrary observed tuples, positive-noise completion and recursive completeness explicitly require positive baseline covariance, exact rank of \(\bar Q\), and inclusion of every shift range in \(\operatorname{range}(\bar Q)\); these follow for tuples generated by the legal causal model but not from a target-block certificate alone.  Signed shifts remain outside the certificate because primitive variance feasibility then depends on unknown baseline structural variances.  The semialgebraic algorithm is a certification route rather than a transcriptome-scale complexity claim, and the exact local power value requires the complete incident tangent geometry.
honest_scope: The aggregate sharp fiber, positive-noise realization, subset recursion, measurable approximate selector, finite-sample family coverage, two-regime information boundary, and four-node collision rate are theorem-level claims.  The finite-sample sufficient threshold remains \(\sqrt{2}m\delta_n(\theta)>2c_{\alpha}+1\) on the stated confidence event, with the full \(x\)-indexed bound retained for consistency.  A universal one-variable local envelope is not claimed: the proved negative result gives an explicit geometry-indexed Gaussian optimization and same-distance witness showing that \(c\) alone is insufficient.  When \(r=1\), the aggregate result reduces to the ambiguity \(\{\{j\}:\bar Q_{jj}>0\}\); no stronger single-target identification is asserted.
interpretation: For a Perturb-seq or Sci-Plex panel, each nonbaseline condition may reveal only part of the effective perturbation support.  The aggregate certificate combines those conditions without assigning privileged status to one arm.  Report the full compatible family, its compulsory intersection, and its possible union; interpret a singleton only when the augmented classification image is a singleton.  These labels describe effective variance-shift coordinates in the acyclic covariance model, not direct molecular binding sites, and uncertain or environment-dependent perturbation efficacy should be carried as abstention or a larger family rather than collapsed to a single target.

assumptions.condition: The observed coefficient matrix \(B_{\mu}\) is permutation-similar to a strictly lower-triangular matrix.
For every \(e\in\mathcal E\), the primitive vector \((H_e,\varepsilon_e,\eta_e)\) is centered Gaussian.
For every \(e\in\mathcal E\), the collection consisting of \(H_e\), all coordinates of \(\varepsilon_e\), and \(\eta_e\) is mutually independent.

The covariance of \(\eta_e\) equals the same diagonal matrix \(\Omega_{\eta,\mu}\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\).

definitions.name: legal Gaussian covariance-shift SCM class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{d,E,r}=\{\mu_{d,E,r}: B_{\mu}\text{ is acyclic};\ (H_e,\varepsilon_e,\eta_e)\text{ obey the centered Gaussian and independence conditions};\ \operatorname{Cov}(H_e)=\Omega_{H,\mu};\ \operatorname{Cov}(\eta_e)=\Omega_{\eta,\mu};\ \omega_{0,\mu}>0;\ \Omega_{\eta,\mu}\succ0;\ |T_{\mu}|=r;\ \lambda_{ej}=0\text{ off }T_{\mu};\ \lambda_{ej}\ge0\text{ on }T_{\mu};\ \forall j\in T_{\mu}\ \exists e\in\{1,\ldots,E\}:\lambda_{ej}>0\}\).

definitions.name: ordered LDL certificate
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\iff [\,t\text{ orders }T,\ \bar Q_{tt}\succ0,\ \bar Q_{tt}=L_tD_tL_t^{\mathsf T},\ L_t\text{ unit lower triangular},\ D_t\text{ diagonal positive},\ \Lambda_{e,t}=L_t^{-1}P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T}L_t^{-\mathsf T}\text{ diagonal and entrywise nonnegative for every }1\le e\le E\,]\), where \(\bar Q=\sum_{e=1}^E\Delta_e\) and \(\bar Q_{tt}=P_t\bar QP_t^{\mathsf T}\).

definitions.name: causal target fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)=\{T\subseteq\mathcal V:|T|=r,\ \exists\mu\in\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\text{ with }T_{\mu}=T\text{ and }\operatorname{Cov}_{\mu}(Y_e)=\Sigma_e\text{ for every }e\in\mathcal E\}\).

definitions.name: positive-noise SCM completion
definitions.construction: Given \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\), set \(W_t=\bar QP_t^{\mathsf T}\bar Q_{tt}^{-1}\), \(A_t=W_tL_t\), \(U_t=\begin{psmallmatrix}L_t&0\\A_{t,T^c}&I_{d-r}\end{psmallmatrix}\) after placing \(t\) first, and \(B_t=I_d-U_t^{-1}\).  Choose \(0<\tau<\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_0)/(2(\lVert U_t\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2+1))\), set \(R_0=\Sigma_0-\tau U_tU_t^{\mathsf T}-\tau I_d\), and set \(C_t=U_t^{-1}R_0^{1/2}\).  Take \(H_e\sim N(0,I_d)\), baseline structural and measurement covariances \(\tau I_d\), and in environment \(e\) place the increments \(\operatorname{diag}(\Lambda_{e,t})\) on \(t\) and zero increments off \(T\).

definitions.name: subset-memoized global pivot recursion
definitions.construction: Initialize \(S=\varnothing\), \(R_S=\bar Q=\sum_{e=1}^E\Delta_e\), and \(M_{e,S}=\Delta_e\).  A label \(j\notin S\) is admissible when \(q=(R_S)_{jj}>0\), \(m_e=(M_{e,S})_{jj}\ge0\), and \(q(M_{e,S})_{:j}=m_e(R_S)_{:j}\) for every \(1\le e\le E\).  With \(u=(R_S)_{:j}/q\), update \(R_{S\cup\{j\}}=R_S-quu^{\mathsf T}\) and \(M_{e,S\cup\{j\}}=M_{e,S}-m_euu^{\mathsf T}\), memoizing only \(S\cup\{j\}\).

definitions.name: compulsory-and-possible classification
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C(\theta)=\bigcap_{T\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)}T\), \(\mathcal P(\theta)=\bigcup_{T\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)}T\), and \(h(\theta)=(\mathcal C(\theta),\mathcal P(\theta))\).

definitions.name: bounded legal covariance class
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_K=\{\zeta_{d,E,r}:mI_d\preceq Z_e\preceq MI_d\text{ for every }e\in\mathcal E;\ \operatorname{rank}(\sum_{f=1}^E(Z_f-Z_0))=r;\ \operatorname{range}(Z_e-Z_0)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(\sum_{f=1}^E(Z_f-Z_0))\text{ for every }1\le e\le E;\ \exists T,t\text{ with }|T|=r\text{ and }\operatorname{Cert}(\zeta,T,t)\}\).

definitions.name: certified approximate covariance selector
definitions.construction: Fix a cylindrical algebraic decomposition of the semialgebraic graph \(G_{\epsilon}\) together with its ordered-certificate witness variables, and let \(s_{\epsilon}(s)\) be the definable-choice section obtained by taking the first nonempty cell in that fixed decomposition.

definitions.name: augmented target-family confidence region
definitions.construction: \(W_n=\{\zeta:mI_d\preceq Z_e\preceq MI_d,\ \lVert\zeta-\widehat\Sigma\rVert_w\le c_{\alpha}\}\), \(\widetilde\theta_n=s_1(\widehat\Sigma)\), \(R_n=W_n\cup\{\widetilde\theta_n\}\), \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{out},n}=\bigcup_{\zeta\in R_n\cap\Theta_K}\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\zeta)\), and \(\mathcal H_n=\{h(\zeta):\zeta\in R_n\cap\Theta_K\}\).

definitions.name: four-node profile-collision path
definitions.construction: For \(d=4\), \(r=2\), and \(E=2\), take \(a=(1,1,2,1)^{\mathsf T}\), \(b=(0,1,1,2)^{\mathsf T}\), \(\Sigma_0=I_4\), \(\Delta_1=aa^{\mathsf T}+bb^{\mathsf T}\), and \(\Delta_2(\gamma)=2aa^{\mathsf T}+(2+\gamma)bb^{\mathsf T}\).  Set \(\Sigma_e=\Sigma_0+\Delta_e\), \(\theta_\gamma=(\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2)\), and \(\bar Q=\Delta_1+\Delta_2=3aa^{\mathsf T}+(3+\gamma)bb^{\mathsf T}\).

definitions.name: signed-shift and split-reference boundary witnesses
definitions.construction: For \(d=3\), \(r=2\), and \(E=2\), set \(B_{\mu}=0\), \(C_{\mu}=0\), \(\omega_{0,\mu}=(3/2,3/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T}\), \(\Omega_{\eta,\mu}=I_3/2\), and \(T_{\mu}=\{1,2\}\).  Define \(\theta^{\pm}\) by \(\lambda_1=(1,1,0)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\lambda_2=(-1/2,0,0)^{\mathsf T}\), so \(\Sigma_0=2I_3\), \(\Sigma_1=\operatorname{diag}(3,3,2)\), and \(\Sigma_2=\operatorname{diag}(3/2,2,2)\).  Define \(\theta^{\mathrm{split}}\) by \(\lambda_1=(1,0,0)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\lambda_2=(0,1,0)^{\mathsf T}\), so \(\Sigma_0=2I_3\), \(\Sigma_1=\operatorname{diag}(3,2,2)\), and \(\Sigma_2=\operatorname{diag}(2,3,2)\).

definitions.name: geometry-indexed local collision power-envelope handle
definitions.construction: For a specified regular sequence, first derive its Gaussian local experiment and record its tangent geometry as \(\mathcal G=(k,g_0,\mathcal A)\), where \(X\sim N(g,I_k)\), \(g_0\) has the focal complete classification, and \(\mathcal A\) is the union of tangent sets having a different complete classification.  Define the geometry-indexed honest focal-certification value by \(\beta^{\star}_{\mathcal G}(\alpha)=\sup\{\mathbb E_{g_0}\phi(X):\phi:\mathbb R^k\to[0,1]\text{ is Borel and }\sup_{g\in\mathcal A}\mathbb E_g\phi(X)\le\alpha\}\).  Record \(c=\inf_{g\in\mathcal A}\lVert g-g_0\rVert_2\) as the nearest-boundary summary, but retain \(\mathcal G\) as an argument of the envelope.

statements.statement: If \(\operatorname{rank}(Q)=r\), \(Q_{tt}\) is invertible, \(W_t=QP_t^{\mathsf T}Q_{tt}^{-1}\), and \(N=N^{\mathsf T}\) satisfies \(\operatorname{range}(N)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Q)\), then \(N=W_t(P_tNP_t^{\mathsf T})W_t^{\mathsf T}\).
statements.justification: The lemma upgrades target-block diagonalization to an identity for every full covariance shift.
statements.gap: BACKSHIFT and coroICA use global diagonalizers; neither isolates the coordinate-restriction inverse needed for a labeled principal-block converse.
statements.consumer: The positive-noise realization theorem uses this identity to reconstruct every full shift from its target block.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{range}(Q)\) and \(K=QP_t^{\mathsf T}\).  Since \(P_tK=Q_{tt}\) is invertible, the \(r\) columns of \(K\) are linearly independent.  The rank assumption \(\operatorname{rank}(Q)=r\) therefore gives \(\operatorname{range}(K)=\mathcal S\).  Moreover,
\[
 P_tW_t=P_tQP_t^{\mathsf T}Q_{tt}^{-1}=I_r,
 \qquad \operatorname{range}(W_t)\subseteq\mathcal S.
\]
Thus \(W_t\) is the inverse of the restriction \(P_t\vert_{\mathcal S}:\mathcal S\to\mathbb R^r\), and consequently
\[
 W_tP_tx=x\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal S. \tag{1}
\]
Every column of \(N\) belongs to \(\mathcal S\) by the stated range condition, so (1), applied columnwise, gives \(W_tP_tN=N\).  Since \(N=N^{\mathsf T}\), transposing this equality gives \(NP_t^{\mathsf T}W_t^{\mathsf T}=N\).  Hence
\[
 W_t(P_tNP_t^{\mathsf T})W_t^{\mathsf T}
 =(W_tP_tN)P_t^{\mathsf T}W_t^{\mathsf T}
 =NP_t^{\mathsf T}W_t^{\mathsf T}=N,
\]
which proves the claim.  No positivity condition on \(N\) was used.

statements.statement: Suppose \(\Sigma_0\succ0\), \(\operatorname{rank}(\bar Q)=r\), and \(\operatorname{range}(\Delta_e)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(\bar Q)\) for every \(1\le e\le E\), where \(\bar Q=\sum_{e=1}^E\Delta_e\).  For every \(T\subseteq\mathcal V\) and ordering \(t\) satisfying \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\), the construction in \(\text{def:positive-noise-completion}\) yields a model in \(\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\) with target set \(T\), covariance \(\operatorname{Cov}(Y_e)=\Sigma_e\) for all \(e\in\mathcal E\), strictly positive baseline structural-noise variances, and strictly positive stationary measurement-error variances.
statements.justification: The theorem proves that every aggregate certificate has a legal acyclic SCM witness at the actually observed positive-definite baseline.
statements.gap: Existing mixing-matrix and measurement-error results do not provide this arbitrary-baseline positive-noise lift from target-block covariance certificates.
statements.consumer: Every member of the reported family is a realizable causal explanation rather than only an algebraic factorization.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(T\) and an ordering \(t\) for which \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\) holds.  Write \(W=W_t\), \(L=L_t\), \(D=D_t\), and \(A=WL\).  The aggregate certificate and the definitions give
\[
 P_tA=P_t\bar QP_t^{\mathsf T}\bar Q_{tt}^{-1}L=L,
 \qquad
 P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T}=L\Lambda_{e,t}L^{\mathsf T}. \tag{1}
\]
The hypotheses \(\operatorname{rank}(\bar Q)=r\) and \(\operatorname{range}(\Delta_e)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(\bar Q)\) are explicit premises of the narrowed statement.  Apply \(\text{lem:range-reconstruction}\), with its carrier symbol interpreted as \(\bar Q\), first to \(N=\bar Q\) and then to \(N=\Delta_e\).  Because \(\bar Q_{tt}=LDL^{\mathsf T}\), equation (1) yields
\[
 \bar Q=W\bar Q_{tt}W^{\mathsf T}=ADA^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \Delta_e=W(P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T})W^{\mathsf T}
 =A\Lambda_{e,t}A^{\mathsf T}. \tag{2}
\]
Every \(\Delta_e\) is therefore positive semidefinite, since every \(\Lambda_{e,t}\) is diagonal and entrywise nonnegative.

The aggregate identity is also needed to verify target coverage.  Summing the definition of \(\Lambda_{e,t}\) over \(e\) gives
\[
 \sum_{e=1}^E\Lambda_{e,t}
 =L^{-1}P_t\bar QP_t^{\mathsf T}L^{-\mathsf T}
 =L^{-1}(LDL^{\mathsf T})L^{-\mathsf T}=D. \tag{3}
\]
Thus, for each \(1\le k\le r\), the nonnegative numbers \((\Lambda_{e,t})_{kk}\) sum to \(D_{kk}>0\).  Consequently at least one environment has \((\Lambda_{e,t})_{kk}>0\).  This proves the target-coverage condition without requiring a single environment to change every target.

Permute the observed coordinates so that \(t_1,\ldots,t_r\) occur first.  Write \(A_{T^c}\) for the remaining rows of \(A\), and define
\[
 U=\begin{pmatrix}L&0\\ A_{T^c}&I_{d-r}\end{pmatrix}. \tag{4}
\]
By (1), the first \(r\) columns of \(U\) are exactly \(A\).  The matrix \(U\) is unit lower triangular and invertible.  Solving \(UX=I_d\) successively by rows shows that \(U^{-1}\) is unit lower triangular.  Hence \(B=I_d-U^{-1}\) is strictly lower triangular in this permutation, so it is an acyclic observed structural matrix.  Undoing the permutation retains the original observed labels.

Let \(a_0=\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_0)>0\), using the explicit premise \(\Sigma_0\succ0\), and choose \(\tau\) as in \(\text{def:positive-noise-completion}\).  For every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 x^{\mathsf T}R_0x
 &=x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_0x-\tau\lVert U^{\mathsf T}x\rVert_2^2-\tau\lVert x\rVert_2^2\\
 &\ge\bigl(a_0-\tau(\lVert U\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2+1)\bigr)\lVert x\rVert_2^2
 >\frac{a_0}{2}\lVert x\rVert_2^2.
 \end{aligned} \tag{5}
\]
Thus \(R_0\succ0\).  Its spectral decomposition supplies the unique symmetric positive square root \(R_0^{1/2}\).

For each environment, take mutually independent random vectors
\[
 H_e\sim N(0,I_d),\qquad
 \eta_e\sim N(0,\tau I_d),\qquad
 \varepsilon_e\sim N\!\left(0,\tau I_d+
 \operatorname{diag}_t(\Lambda_{e,t})\right), \tag{6}
\]
where \(\operatorname{diag}_t(\Lambda_{e,t})\) places the diagonal entries on the labels in \(t\), is zero off \(T\), and \(\Lambda_{0,t}=0\).  Set \(C=U^{-1}R_0^{1/2}\).  Equation (6) supplies centered Gaussian primitives and the required mutual independence.  The latent covariance \(I_d\), loading \(C\), and measurement covariance \(\tau I_d\succ0\) are invariant over environments.  The baseline structural variance vector is \(\tau\mathbf 1_d>0\).  Its increments vanish off \(T\), are nonnegative on \(T\), and, by (3), every label in \(T\) has a strictly positive increment in at least one environment.  Thus the changing-coordinate set is exactly the declared size-\(r\) set \(T\).

At baseline, independence and the definition of \(Y_e\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_0)
 =UCC^{\mathsf T}U^{\mathsf T}+\tau UU^{\mathsf T}+\tau I_d
 =R_0+\tau UU^{\mathsf T}+\tau I_d=\Sigma_0. \tag{7}
\]
Only the structural-noise covariance changes across environments.  Since the target columns of \(U\) equal \(A\), equations (2) and (7) imply
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_e)-\operatorname{Cov}(Y_0)
 =A\Lambda_{e,t}A^{\mathsf T}=\Delta_e,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_e)=\Sigma_0+\Delta_e=\Sigma_e. \tag{8}
\]
All conditions of the repaired \(\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\), including strict structural and measurement-noise positivity and aggregate target coverage, have now been verified from the construction.

statements.statement: For every covariance tuple \(\theta\) satisfying \(\Sigma_0\succ0\), \(\operatorname{rank}(\bar Q)=r\), and \(\operatorname{range}(\Delta_e)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(\bar Q)\) for all \(1\le e\le E\), where \(\bar Q=\sum_{e=1}^E\Delta_e\), one has \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)\).  Equivalently, a labeled size-\(r\) set is compatible if and only if some ordering has a positive-definite aggregate principal block whose unique unit-lower \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factor simultaneously transforms every target-block shift to a diagonal entrywise-nonnegative matrix.
statements.proof_tex:
We prove the two inclusions without identifying the causal target with the observable certificate by definition.

First let \(T\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\), and choose its witnessing model \(\mu\in\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\).  Set \(U=U_{\mu}\), and order all observed labels topologically so that \(U=(I_d-B_{\mu})^{-1}\) is unit lower triangular.  Let \(t\) be the induced order on the target labels and put \(A=UP_t^{\mathsf T}\), the matrix of target columns of \(U\).  Stationarity of \(H_e\) and \(\eta_e\), mutual independence of the primitive blocks, and absence of off-target shifts give, for every \(e\ge1\),
\[
 \Delta_e
 =U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_e)U^{\mathsf T}
 =A\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{e,t_1},\ldots,\lambda_{e,t_r})A^{\mathsf T}. \tag{8}
\]
The target principal submatrix \(P_tA=U_{tt}\) is unit lower triangular: it is a principal submatrix of \(U\) with its indices retained in topological order.  By the common-reference assumption, all reference coefficients in (8) are strictly positive.  Consequently
\[
 Q_{tt}=U_{tt}\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{1,t_1},\ldots,\lambda_{1,t_r})U_{tt}^{\mathsf T}\succ0. \tag{9}
\]
The positive unit-lower \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factorization is unique.  To verify the only fact used here, compare two such factorizations and their \((1,1)\) entries and first columns; these determine the first diagonal pivot and the entries below it.  Subtracting that rank-one term leaves the corresponding \((r-1)\)-dimensional factorizations, so induction determines every column and pivot.  Applying this uniqueness to (9) gives
\[
 L_t=U_{tt},\qquad
 D_t=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{1,t_1},\ldots,\lambda_{1,t_r}). \tag{10}
\]
Taking the \(t\)-principal block of (8) and using (10),
\[
 \Lambda_{e,t}
 =L_t^{-1}P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T}L_t^{-\mathsf T}
 =\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{e,t_1},\ldots,\lambda_{e,t_r}), \tag{11}
\]
which is diagonal and entrywise nonnegative by \(\text{ass:nonnegative-variance-shifts}\).  Thus \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\) holds, proving
\(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\subseteq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)\).

Conversely, if \(T\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)\), then \(\text{def:algebraic-target-fiber}\) supplies an ordering \(t\) with \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\).  The hypotheses of \(\text{thm:positive-noise-realization}\) are precisely the baseline positivity, exact reference rank, and common shift range assumed here.  That theorem constructs a model \(\mu\in\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\) with \(T_{\mu}=T\) and covariance tuple \(\theta\).  Hence \(T\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\), proving the reverse inclusion.  Combining the inclusions yields the equality of fibers.  Finally, expanding \(\text{def:algebraic-target-fiber}\) and \(\text{def:ordered-ldl-certificate}\) gives exactly the stated necessary-and-sufficient ordered principal-block recovery map.
statements.justification: This is the necessary-and-sufficient population kernel that replaces nonsharp target supersets by the complete labeled fiber.
statements.gap: Yang, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash characterize a superset under latent confounding, while BACKSHIFT and coroICA identify a global mixing matrix only when variance profiles separate; none characterizes all labeled acyclic target sets at profile collisions.
statements.consumer: Unknown-target perturbation studies can report all and only covariance-compatible effective target sets while retaining stationary latent confounding and measurement error.

statements.statement: Suppose \(\Sigma_0\succ0\), \(\operatorname{rank}(\bar Q)=r\), and \(\operatorname{range}(\Delta_e)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(\bar Q)\) for every \(1\le e\le E\), where \(\bar Q=\sum_{e=1}^E\Delta_e\).  The leaves of depth \(r\) accepted by the recursion in \(\text{def:subset-pivot-recursion}\) are exactly \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\).  Every reached residual pair \((R_S,(M_{e,S})_{e=1}^{E})\) depends only on \(S\), so the algorithm terminates after visiting at most \(\sum_{k=0}^{r}\binom{d}{k}\) subset states, and the intersection and union of its leaves equal \(\mathcal C(\theta)\) and \(\mathcal P(\theta)\).
statements.justification: The aggregate residual recursion converts the sharp characterization into a terminating complete-family algorithm with subset memoization.
statements.gap: No prior covariance-shift method supplies this complete labeled pivot enumeration at profile collisions.
statements.consumer: The leaves directly yield compulsory and possible effective targets together with witness orderings.
statements.proof_tex:
We first prove the order-independent residual formula.  For a reached subset \(S\), let
\[
 E_S=I_d-\bar Q_{:S}\bar Q_{SS}^{-1}P_S. \tag{15}
\]
All preceding aggregate pivots are positive, so elimination gives a unit-lower factorization of \(\bar Q_{SS}\) with positive diagonal pivots; hence \(\bar Q_{SS}\succ0\) and the inverse in (15) exists.  Direct multiplication, using \(P_S\bar Q_{:S}=\bar Q_{SS}\), gives
\[
 E_S\bar Q=\bar QE_S^{\mathsf T}
 =\bar Q-\bar Q_{:S}\bar Q_{SS}^{-1}\bar Q_{S:},
 \qquad E_S\bar QE_S^{\mathsf T}=E_S\bar Q. \tag{16}
\]
Therefore the residuals defined in the recursion satisfy
\[
 R_S=\bar Q-\bar Q_{:S}\bar Q_{SS}^{-1}\bar Q_{S:},
 \qquad M_{e,S}=E_S\Delta_eE_S^{\mathsf T}. \tag{17}
\]
If (17) holds and \(j\notin S\) is accepted, put \(q=(R_S)_{jj}>0\) and \(u=(R_S)_{:j}/q\).  The scalar block-inverse identity for \(\bar Q_{S\cup\{j\},S\cup\{j\}}\) changes the first expression in (17) to
\(R_S-quu^{\mathsf T}\).  The same elimination applied to the second expression, together with
\((M_{e,S})_{:j}=m_eu\), changes it to \(M_{e,S}-m_euu^{\mathsf T}\).  These are exactly the recursion updates.  Induction from \(S=\varnothing\) proves (17) at every reached subset, so the residual tuple depends only on \(S\).

Suppose next that \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\) certifies \(T\).  By \(\text{lem:range-reconstruction}\), applied with aggregate carrier \(\bar Q\), and with \(A=W_tL_t\),
\[
 \bar Q=\sum_{k=1}^r d_ka_ka_k^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \Delta_e=\sum_{k=1}^r \ell_{ek}a_ka_k^{\mathsf T}, \tag{18}
\]
where \(a_k\) is column \(k\) of \(A\), \(d_k=(D_t)_{kk}>0\), and \(\ell_{ek}=(\Lambda_{e,t})_{kk}\ge0\).  Since \(P_tA=L_t\),
\[
 (a_k)_{t_i}=0\quad(i<k),\qquad (a_k)_{t_k}=1. \tag{19}
\]
After the first \(k-1\) updates, equations (18)--(19) imply inductively
\[
 R=\sum_{l=k}^r d_la_la_l^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad M_e=\sum_{l=k}^r\ell_{el}a_la_l^{\mathsf T}. \tag{20}
\]
At label \(t_k\), one has \(q=d_k>0\), \(m_e=\ell_{ek}\ge0\), \(R_{:t_k}=d_ka_k\), and \((M_e)_{:t_k}=\ell_{ek}a_k\).  Hence the proportionality equation holds and every certifying ordering is an accepted depth-\(r\) path.

Conversely, let \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\) be an accepted path, with successive values \(q_k>0\), \(m_{ek}\ge0\), and \(u_k\).  The explicit aggregate-range premise implies
\[
 \operatorname{range}(M_{e,S})\subseteq\operatorname{range}(R_S). \tag{21}
\]
To justify (21), symmetry and \(\operatorname{range}(\Delta_e)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(\bar Q)\) permit the factorization
\(\Delta_e=\bar Q C_e\bar Q\), for example with
\(C_e=\bar Q^{+}\Delta_e\bar Q^{+}\), where \(\bar Q^{+}\) is the Moore--Penrose inverse.  Indeed, \(P=\bar Q\bar Q^{+}\) is the orthogonal projection onto \(\operatorname{range}(\bar Q)\); range inclusion gives \(P\Delta_e=\Delta_e\), symmetry gives \(\Delta_eP=\Delta_e\), and therefore \(\bar QC_e\bar Q=P\Delta_eP=\Delta_e\).  Equations (16)--(17) then give
\(M_{e,S}=R_SC_eR_S\), proving the range inclusion.

The Schur-complement rank identity in (17) shows that each nonzero pivot lowers \(\operatorname{rank}(R_S)\) by one.  Since \(\operatorname{rank}(\bar Q)=r\), after \(r\) accepted pivots \(R_T=0\), and (21) then implies \(M_{e,T}=0\).  Telescoping the updates gives
\[
 \bar Q=\sum_{k=1}^r q_ku_ku_k^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \Delta_e=\sum_{k=1}^r m_{ek}u_ku_k^{\mathsf T}. \tag{22}
\]
Every residual has zero rows and columns at earlier selected labels.  Thus \((u_k)_{t_i}=0\) for \(i<k\), while \((u_k)_{t_k}=1\).  If
\(L=P_t[u_1\ \cdots\ u_r]\), then \(L\) is unit lower triangular, and (22) yields
\[
 \bar Q_{tt}=L\operatorname{diag}(q_1,\ldots,q_r)L^{\mathsf T}\succ0,
 \qquad
 L^{-1}P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T}L^{-\mathsf T}
 =\operatorname{diag}(m_{e1},\ldots,m_{er})\succeq0. \tag{23}
\]
Hence \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\) holds.  The depth-\(r\) leaves are exactly \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)\), and the baseline, aggregate-rank, and aggregate-range premises allow \(\text{thm:sharp-target-fiber}\) to identify this family with \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\).

There are at most \(\binom dk\) memoized subsets at depth \(k\), hence at most \(\sum_{k=0}^r\binom dk\) states.  The recursion stops at depth \(r\).  Finally, the complete-classification definition identifies the intersection and union of the exact leaf family with \(\mathcal C(\theta)\) and \(\mathcal P(\theta)\), respectively.

statements.statement: For every \(\epsilon>0\), the correspondence \(G_{\epsilon}\) admits a semialgebraic, hence Borel measurable, section \(s_{\epsilon}\) that returns both \(s_{\epsilon}(s)\in\Theta_K\) and an ordered certificate witness, with \(\lVert s_{\epsilon}(s)-s\rVert_w<\inf_{\zeta\in\Theta_K}\lVert\zeta-s\rVert_w+\epsilon\) for every covariance statistic \(s\).
statements.justification: This closes the nonattainment gap created by exact rank and strict positive pivots without assuming a nearest model point exists.
statements.gap: Brown and Purves treat measurable attained extrema, and Romano and Shaikh invert criteria over identified sets; neither supplies certified approximate projection through this nonclosed exact-rank semialgebraic covariance model.
statements.consumer: The augmented confidence construction needs this selector to be measurable and nonempty on every sample, including off-model empirical covariances.
statements.proof_tex:
We first verify that the feasible set is nonempty; this is required because an approximate minimizer cannot otherwise be selected.  Let
\[
 a=\frac{m+M}{2},\qquad q=\frac{M-m}{4},\qquad
 Z_0=aI_d,\qquad Z_1=Z_0+q\operatorname{diag}(I_r,0),\qquad Z_e=Z_0\ (e\ge2).
\]
Because \(0<m<M\), all eigenvalues lie in \([m,M]\).  The reference difference has rank \(r\), every later difference has range in its range, and the first \(r\) labels with their natural order have certificate \(L=I_r\), \(D=qI_r\), \(\Lambda_1=qI_r\), and \(\Lambda_e=0\) for \(e\ge2\).  Thus this tuple belongs to \(\Theta_K\).

Next we expose the finite-dimensional real-algebraic structure rather than assuming an attained projection.  Positive semidefiniteness and positive definiteness are finite principal-minor inequalities.  Exact rank \(r\) is expressed by vanishing of all \((r+1)\)-minors and strict positivity of the sum of squares of all \(r\)-minors.  Given exact reference rank \(r\), the common-range condition is expressed by vanishing of all \((r+1)\)-minors of the matrices obtained by adjoining columns of \(Z_e-Z_0\) to \(Z_1-Z_0\).  For each of the finitely many choices of \(T\) and \(t\), the certificate is expressed using real witness variables \(L,D,(\Lambda_e)_e\), the polynomial equations
\[
 Q_{tt}=LDL^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 P_t(Z_e-Z_0)P_t^{\mathsf T}=L\Lambda_eL^{\mathsf T}, \tag{20}
\]
together with unit-lower and diagonal zero equations, strict positivity of the diagonal of \(D\), and nonnegativity of the diagonals of \(\Lambda_e\).  Hence membership in \(\Theta_K\), with one ordered witness retained, is a finite Boolean combination of polynomial equalities and inequalities after existentially eliminating the displayed witness variables.

Let
\[
 v(s)=\inf_{\xi\in\Theta_K}\lVert\xi-s\rVert_w^2.
\]
It is finite because \(\Theta_K\ne\varnothing\).  Its graph is characterized without attainment by
\[
 v\ge0,\qquad
 \bigl(\forall\xi\in\Theta_K\bigr)\ v\le\lVert\xi-s\rVert_w^2,\qquad
 \bigl(\forall u>v\bigr)\bigl(\exists\xi\in\Theta_K\bigr)\
       \lVert\xi-s\rVert_w^2<u. \tag{21}
\]
All expressions in (21) are polynomial after expanding the weighted Frobenius norm.  A cylindrical algebraic decomposition eliminates the quantified coordinates in (20)--(21), so the graph of \(v\) and the augmented graph consisting of
\((s,\zeta,T,t,L,D,(\Lambda_e)_e)\) satisfying (20), \(\zeta\in\Theta_K\), and
\[
 \lVert\zeta-s\rVert_w^2<\bigl(\sqrt{v(s)}+\epsilon\bigr)^2 \tag{22}
\]
are semialgebraic; the square root in (22) is encoded by an auxiliary \(\rho\ge0\) with \(\rho^2=v(s)\).  Every fiber of this augmented graph is nonempty.  Indeed, by the defining property of an infimum, for every \(\epsilon>0\) some \(\zeta\in\Theta_K\) has \(\lVert\zeta-s\rVert_w<\sqrt{v(s)}+\epsilon\), and membership supplies one of the finitely many ordered witnesses.

It remains to justify the section asserted by \(\text{def:certified-approximate-selector}\).  In the fixed cylindrical decomposition, order the finitely many cells.  Over each base cell choose the first cell having a nonempty fiber.  A cylindrical cell in one new coordinate is either the graph of one of its semialgebraic boundary functions or a band between two such functions.  Select the boundary value in the graph case, the midpoint for two finite boundaries, the lower boundary plus one or the upper boundary minus one for a one-sided band, and zero for a two-sided unbounded band.  Repeating this coordinate by coordinate produces a semialgebraic point in the chosen fiber.  Induction over the finitely many coordinates gives a semialgebraic section of the augmented graph, including the discrete ordered-certificate branch.  Its covariance component is the map \(s_{\epsilon}\).

By construction,
\[
 s_{\epsilon}(s)\in\Theta_K,\qquad
 \lVert s_{\epsilon}(s)-s\rVert_w
 <\inf_{\xi\in\Theta_K}\lVert\xi-s\rVert_w+\epsilon, \tag{23}
\]
and the retained variables satisfy (20), hence certify the returned tuple.  Finally, a semialgebraic map is Borel measurable: the inverse image of an open coordinate box is the projection of its semialgebraic graph intersected with that box, hence is semialgebraic by the same cylindrical elimination, and coordinate boxes generate the Euclidean Borel sigma-field.  This proves all parts of the lemma without assuming that the infimum in (21) is attained.

statements.statement: Under the independent Gaussian sampling design, uniformly over \(\theta\in\Theta_K\), \(\Pr_{\theta}[\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\subseteq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{out},n}\text{ and }h(\theta)\in\mathcal H_n]\ge1-\alpha\).  The region \(R_n\cap\Theta_K\) is nonempty for every sample, and a rule reports a classification only when \(\mathcal H_n\) is a singleton has probability at most \(\alpha\) of reporting a classification different from \(h(\theta)\).
statements.justification: Family coverage must retain structural uncertainty and remain well-defined when the raw covariance region misses the nonclosed model.
statements.gap: Strieder et al. retain graph uncertainty by test inversion and Romano--Shaikh cover identified sets, but neither gives always-nonempty coverage of a discontinuous discrete target family under exact-rank covariance restrictions.
statements.consumer: A Perturb-seq or Sci-Plex audit can abstain near collisions while maintaining finite-sample coverage of all effective target explanations under the stated covariance model.
statements.proof_tex:
For a fixed environment suppress the index \(e\), write
\(\widehat\Sigma=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nY_iY_i^{\mathsf T}\), and diagonalize
\(\Sigma=O\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_d)O^{\mathsf T}\).  Writing \(Y=O\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\sigma_j})Z\) with independent standard normal coordinates, differentiation of the one-dimensional moment generating function gives
\(\mathbb E Z_j^2=1\), \(\mathbb E Z_j^4=3\), and independence gives
\[
 \mathbb E(Y_jY_kY_lY_m)
 =\Sigma_{jk}\Sigma_{lm}+\Sigma_{jl}\Sigma_{km}+\Sigma_{jm}\Sigma_{kl}. \tag{24}
\]
Consequently, independence across observations and a direct sum over matrix entries yield
\[
 \mathbb E_{\Sigma}\lVert\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma\rVert_F^2
 =\frac1n\sum_{j,k}\operatorname{Var}(Y_jY_k)
 =\frac1n\left\{(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma)^2+\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma^2)\right\}. \tag{25}
\]
Under \(\Sigma\preceq MI_d\), the right side multiplied by \(n\) is at most
\(M^2(d^2+d)=M^2d(d+1)\).  Summing (25) over the independent environments proves, uniformly over \(\theta\in\Theta_K\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{\theta}\lVert\widehat\Sigma-\theta\rVert_w^2
 \le(E+1)M^2d(d+1)=V_{\max}. \tag{26}
\]
Markov's inequality and \(c_{\alpha}^2=V_{\max}/\alpha\) therefore give
\[
 \Pr_{\theta}\!\left(\lVert\widehat\Sigma-\theta\rVert_w\le c_{\alpha}\right)
 \ge1-\alpha. \tag{27}
\]

On the event in (27), the true tuple satisfies the covariance box constraints and belongs to \(W_n\), so
\(\theta\in R_n\cap\Theta_K\).  The sharp-fiber theorem gives
\(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)\).  Since the latter family is one of the terms in the union defining \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{out},n}\), and \(h(\theta)\) is one of the values defining \(\mathcal H_n\),
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\subseteq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{out},n},
 \qquad h(\theta)\in\mathcal H_n. \tag{28}
\]
Combining (27)--(28) proves the asserted uniform joint coverage.

For every sample, \(\text{lem:measurable-certified-selection}\), with \(\epsilon=1\), gives
\(\widetilde\theta_n=s_1(\widehat\Sigma)\in\Theta_K\).  Since this point is included in \(R_n\), the intersection \(R_n\cap\Theta_K\) is never empty.  The selector is Borel measurable.  Moreover, membership of any fixed target set or fixed value of \(h\) in the reported objects is an existential statement over the semialgebraic certificate and region constraints; cylindrical elimination makes each such event Borel.  Thus the finite-valued reporting rule is measurable.

Finally, suppose the rule reports a singleton classification different from \(h(\theta)\).  On the event in (27), (28) puts \(h(\theta)\) in \(\mathcal H_n\), so a singleton \(\mathcal H_n\) could only equal \(\{h(\theta)\}\).  An incorrect report is therefore contained in the complement of (27), whose probability is at most \(\alpha\).  This proves the finite-sample honesty statement.

statements.statement: For every \(x>0\), on the event \(\lVert\widehat\Sigma-\theta\rVert_w\le x\), every point of \(R_n\) is within weighted distance at most \(\max\{x+c_{\alpha},2x+1\}\) of \(\theta\).  Hence, if \(\max\{x+c_{\alpha},2x+1\}<\sqrt{2}m\delta_n(\theta)\), the singleton rule based on \(\mathcal H_n\) reports \(h(\theta)\), and its failure probability is at most \(V_{\max}/x^2\).  In particular, \(\sqrt{2}m\delta_n(\theta)>2c_{\alpha}+1\) implies correct reporting with probability at least \(1-\alpha\).  For every sequence \(\theta_n\in\Theta_K\) with \(\delta_n(\theta_n)\to\infty\), the rule reports \(h(\theta_n)\) with probability tending to one, uniformly over subclasses on which the infimum of \(\delta_n\) diverges.
statements.justification: The result identifies the observable separation scale at which honest abstention disappears.
statements.gap: Lewis studies weak heteroskedastic identification for continuous structural parameters; the present boundary concerns the entire discrete compulsory-and-possible target classification over a nonclosed causal fiber.
statements.consumer: Analysts obtain a diagnostic for when an exact target classification, rather than an outer family, is statistically defensible.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\theta\in\Theta_K\) and let
\(Z=\lVert\widehat\Sigma-\theta\rVert_w\).  On \(Z\le x\), every \(\zeta\in W_n\) obeys, by the triangle inequality,
\[
 \lVert\zeta-\theta\rVert_w
 \le\lVert\zeta-\widehat\Sigma\rVert_w
   +\lVert\widehat\Sigma-\theta\rVert_w
 \le c_{\alpha}+x. \tag{29}
\]
Because \(\theta\in\Theta_K\), the infimum in the selector inequality is at most \(Z\).  The strict approximate-fit property with tolerance one therefore gives
\[
 \lVert\widetilde\theta_n-\widehat\Sigma\rVert_w<Z+1,
 \qquad
 \lVert\widetilde\theta_n-\theta\rVert_w<2Z+1\le2x+1. \tag{30}
\]
Equations (29)--(30) imply the claimed non-strict bound
\[
 \sup_{\zeta\in R_n}\lVert\zeta-\theta\rVert_w
 \le\max\{x+c_{\alpha},2x+1\}. \tag{31}
\]

For any symmetric tuple \(H=(H_e)_e\) and any \(\theta\in\Theta_K\), put
\(K_e=\Sigma_e^{-1/2}H_e\Sigma_e^{-1/2}\).  Then
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_e^{-1}H_e\Sigma_e^{-1}H_e)=\lVert K_e\rVert_F^2.
\]
Since \(mI_d\preceq\Sigma_e\preceq MI_d\), the identities
\(H_e=\Sigma_e^{1/2}K_e\Sigma_e^{1/2}\) and the operator-norm inequality for the Frobenius norm give
\[
 \frac1M\lVert H_e\rVert_F\le\lVert K_e\rVert_F
 \le\frac1m\lVert H_e\rVert_F.
\]
After weighting and summing,
\[
 \frac{1}{\sqrt2 M}\lVert H\rVert_w
 \le\lVert H\rVert_{I,n,\theta}
 \le\frac{1}{\sqrt2 m}\lVert H\rVert_w. \tag{32}
\]

Suppose the strict separation inequality in the theorem holds.  For every
\(\zeta\in R_n\cap\Theta_K\), (31)--(32) imply
\[
 \lVert\zeta-\theta\rVert_{I,n,\theta}
 \le\frac{\lVert\zeta-\theta\rVert_w}{\sqrt2m}
 <\delta_n(\theta). \tag{33}
\]
By the definition of \(\delta_n(\theta)\), no point satisfying (33) can belong to
\(\mathcal A_h(\theta)\).  Hence every point in \(R_n\cap\Theta_K\) has classification \(h(\theta)\).  This intersection is nonempty by \(\text{thm:honest-family-confidence}\), so
\(\mathcal H_n=\{h(\theta)\}\) and the singleton rule reports correctly.

The moment calculation (24)--(26), applied with threshold \(x\), gives
\[
 \Pr_{\theta}(Z>x)\le \frac{\mathbb EZ^2}{x^2}
 \le\frac{V_{\max}}{x^2}. \tag{34}
\]
This is the asserted failure bound.  Taking \(x=c_{\alpha}\), the radius in (31) is at most
\(2c_{\alpha}+1\), while (34) equals \(\alpha\); this proves the stated finite-sample consequence.

For a sequence with \(\delta_n(\theta_n)\to\infty\), choose deterministic \(x_n\to\infty\) with
\(x_n/\delta_n(\theta_n)\to0\).  Then the strict separation condition holds eventually, whereas (34) tends to zero.  If a subclass satisfies
\(D_n:=\inf_{\theta\text{ in the subclass}}\delta_n(\theta)\to\infty\), the common choice
\(x_n=\sqrt{D_n}\) has the same two properties, proving the asserted uniformity.

statements.statement: The tuple \(\theta^{\pm}\) is generated by an acyclic positive-structural-noise, positive-measurement-noise Gaussian SCM satisfying every member condition of \(\mathcal M_{3,2,2}\) except nonnegative variance shifts, and its true target set is \(\{1,2\}\).  For each ordering of that target, the aggregate ordered certificate has unit-lower factor equal to the identity and its transformed second-environment target block contains the diagonal entry \(-1/2\), so \(\operatorname{Cert}\) rejects the true target.  The tuple \(\theta^{\mathrm{split}}\) is generated by a member of \(\mathcal M_{3,2,2}\) with true target set \(\{1,2\}\); although its designated reference shift \(Q\) has rank one, strictly less than \(r=2\), its aggregate carrier has rank \(r\), and \(\operatorname{Cert}\) accepts the true target in both orders.  Thus signed shifts destroy the nonnegative-diagonal necessity and require baseline-variance feasibility in place of nonnegativity, whereas a common all-target reference is unnecessary for the aggregate-carrier certificate.
statements.justification: The result identifies exactly which parts of the certificate fail when either design restriction is removed.
statements.gap: BACKSHIFT permits signed covariance changes and does not require a designated common reference, whereas the labeled principal-block fiber uses both restrictions; the explicit witnesses prevent that narrower result from being advertised as a general covariance-shift characterization.
statements.consumer: Panel designers learn whether to add a lowest-variance baseline and a broad calibration environment, and analysts without them know which certificate component must be replaced rather than trusted.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(\lambda^{\pm}\) and \(\lambda^{\mathrm{split}}\) for the two increment arrays in \(\text{def:restriction-boundary-witnesses}\), and put \(\lambda^w_0=0\) for \(w\in\{\pm,\mathrm{split}\}\).  We first construct the primitive variables, rather than treating the covariance displays in that definition as proof of SCM compatibility.  For each \(w\), let every coordinate of the vectors \(h_e,z_e,v_e\), over \(e\in\{0,1,2\}\), be mutually independent standard normal random variables, and define
\[
 H_e=h_e,\qquad
 \varepsilon_e=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\sqrt{\omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^w_e}\right)z_e,
 \qquad
 \eta_e=2^{-1/2}v_e. \tag{1}
\]
The square root in (1) is coordinatewise.  For the signed witness, the three structural-variance vectors are
\[
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\pm}_0=(3/2,3/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\pm}_1=(5/2,5/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\pm}_2=(1,3/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T}; \tag{2}
\]
for the split-reference witness, they are
\[
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\mathrm{split}}_0=(3/2,3/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\mathrm{split}}_1=(5/2,3/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 \omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^{\mathrm{split}}_2=(3/2,5/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T}. \tag{3}
\]
Every coordinate in (2) and (3) is strictly positive, so all square roots in (1) exist and every displayed structural-noise covariance is positive definite.

Set \(\Omega_{H,\mu}=I_3\).  Equation (1) gives centered jointly Gaussian primitive vectors.  Their construction gives the mutual independence required by \(\text{def:legal-scm-class}\), the stationary latent covariance \(I_3\), and the stationary diagonal measurement covariance \(I_3/2\succ0\).  The choices in \(\text{def:restriction-boundary-witnesses}\) give \(B_\mu=0\), hence an acyclic observed system and
\[
 U_\mu=(I_3-B_\mu)^{-1}=I_3,
\]
as well as \(C_\mu=0\) and \(\omega_{0,\mu}=(3/2,3/2,3/2)^{\mathsf T}>0\) coordinatewise.  Independence and the definition of \(Y_e\) therefore imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_e)
 &=U_\mu\!\left(C_\mu\Omega_{H,\mu}C_\mu^{\mathsf T}
   +\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^w_e)\right)U_\mu^{\mathsf T}
   +\Omega_{\eta,\mu}\\
 &=\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda^w_e)+\tfrac12 I_3.
 \end{aligned} \tag{4}
\]
Substitution of (2) and (3) into (4) gives exactly the covariance tuples \(\theta^{\pm}\) and \(\theta^{\mathrm{split}}\) declared in \(\text{def:restriction-boundary-witnesses}\).

For \(\theta^{\pm}\), take the structural target set \(T_\mu=\{1,2\}\).  It has cardinality \(2=r\), all increments on coordinate \(3\) vanish, and both coordinates in \(T_\mu\) change because \(\lambda^{\pm}_{11}=\lambda^{\pm}_{12}=1\).  In particular, the target-coverage condition holds: for each \(j\in T_\mu\), environment \(e=1\) has \(\lambda^{\pm}_{1j}>0\).  All member conditions of the aggregate-carrier version of \(\mathcal M_{3,2,2}\) have now been checked except nonnegativity, which fails only because
\[
 \lambda^{\pm}_{21}=-1/2<0. \tag{5}
\]
Notice that (5) does not invalidate the primitive law: by (2), the corresponding structural variance equals \(3/2-1/2=1>0\).  Since the increments are nonzero on exactly the labels \(1\) and \(2\), the causal target of this constructed SCM is \(T_\mu=\{1,2\}\); this conclusion precedes, and does not define that target through, the observable certificate.

By (4), the observable shifts and their aggregate carrier are
\[
 \Delta^{\pm}_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,0),\qquad
 \Delta^{\pm}_2=\operatorname{diag}(-1/2,0,0),\qquad
 \overline Q^{\pm}:=\Delta^{\pm}_1+\Delta^{\pm}_2
   =\operatorname{diag}(1/2,1,0). \tag{6}
\]
Consider first \(t=(1,2)\).  The ordered aggregate principal block is \(\operatorname{diag}(1/2,1)\succ0\).  To identify its positive \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factors without invoking an undeclared uniqueness result, write
\[
 L_t=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\ \ell&1\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad D_t=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,d_2),
 \qquad d_1,d_2>0.
\]
Equating entries in
\[
 L_tD_tL_t^{\mathsf T}
 =\begin{pmatrix}d_1&d_1\ell\\ d_1\ell&d_1\ell^2+d_2\end{pmatrix}
 =\begin{pmatrix}1/2&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\]
gives \(d_1=1/2\), then \(\ell=0\), and then \(d_2=1\).  Thus \(L_t=I_2\), and the transformed second-environment target block is
\[
 L_t^{-1}P_t\Delta^{\pm}_2P_t^{\mathsf T}L_t^{-\mathsf T}
 =\operatorname{diag}(-1/2,0). \tag{7}
\]
It violates the entrywise-nonnegative requirement in \(\text{def:ordered-ldl-certificate}\).  For the only other order \(t'=(2,1)\), the aggregate principal block is \(\operatorname{diag}(1,1/2)\).  The same entry comparison gives \(L_{t'}=I_2\), and the transformed second-environment block is
\[
 L_{t'}^{-1}P_{t'}\Delta^{\pm}_2P_{t'}^{\mathsf T}L_{t'}^{-\mathsf T}
 =\operatorname{diag}(0,-1/2), \tag{8}
\]
which again violates nonnegativity.  Equations (7) and (8) prove that no ordering of the true causal target satisfies \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta^{\pm},\{1,2\},t)\).

For \(\theta^{\mathrm{split}}\), again take \(T_\mu=\{1,2\}\).  The verification preceding (4) establishes acyclicity, Gaussianity, independence, stationarity, and strict positivity of structural and measurement noise.  The target has size \(r=2\), every off-target increment is zero, and every target increment is nonnegative.  Moreover, target coverage holds because coordinate \(1\) has \(\lambda^{\mathrm{split}}_{11}=1>0\) and coordinate \(2\) has \(\lambda^{\mathrm{split}}_{22}=1>0\).  Hence this witness satisfies every member condition of the aggregate-carrier version of \(\mathcal M_{3,2,2}\).  Its changing coordinates are exactly \(1\) and \(2\), so its causal target is \(T_\mu=\{1,2\}\).

The individual shifts satisfy
\[
 Q=\Delta^{\mathrm{split}}_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,0,0),\qquad
 \Delta^{\mathrm{split}}_2=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,0), \tag{9}
\]
and consequently \(\operatorname{rank}(Q)=1<2=r\).  Nevertheless, the corrected aggregate carrier is
\[
 \overline Q^{\mathrm{split}}
 :=\Delta^{\mathrm{split}}_1+\Delta^{\mathrm{split}}_2
 =\operatorname{diag}(1,1,0),
 \qquad \operatorname{rank}(\overline Q^{\mathrm{split}})=2=r. \tag{10}
\]
It also carries every environment-specific range, since
\[
 \operatorname{range}(\Delta^{\mathrm{split}}_1)
 =\operatorname{span}\{(1,0,0)^{\mathsf T}\}
 \subseteq\operatorname{range}(\overline Q^{\mathrm{split}}),
\]
\[
 \operatorname{range}(\Delta^{\mathrm{split}}_2)
 =\operatorname{span}\{(0,1,0)^{\mathsf T}\}
 \subseteq\operatorname{range}(\overline Q^{\mathrm{split}})
 =\operatorname{span}\{(1,0,0)^{\mathsf T},(0,1,0)^{\mathsf T}\}. \tag{11}
\]
For \(t=(1,2)\), the aggregate target block in (10) is \(I_2\).  The preceding entrywise \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) calculation, now with both diagonal entries equal to one, gives \(L_t=D_t=I_2\).  Hence the two transformed blocks are
\[
 L_t^{-1}P_t\Delta^{\mathrm{split}}_1P_t^{\mathsf T}L_t^{-\mathsf T}
 =\operatorname{diag}(1,0),\qquad
 L_t^{-1}P_t\Delta^{\mathrm{split}}_2P_t^{\mathsf T}L_t^{-\mathsf T}
 =\operatorname{diag}(0,1). \tag{12}
\]
They are diagonal and entrywise nonnegative.  For the reversed order \(t'=(2,1)\), the aggregate target block remains \(I_2\), so \(L_{t'}=D_{t'}=I_2\), while the two matrices in (12) are merely interchanged.  Every clause of \(\text{def:ordered-ldl-certificate}\) therefore holds for both orders, proving
\[
 \operatorname{Cert}(\theta^{\mathrm{split}},\{1,2\},(1,2))
 =\operatorname{Cert}(\theta^{\mathrm{split}},\{1,2\},(2,1))
 =\mathrm{true}. \tag{13}
\]

Finally, no single environment of the split witness shifts both target coordinates: the two target profiles are \((1,0)^{\mathsf T}\) and \((0,1)^{\mathsf T}\).  Thus (10)--(13) prove directly that a common all-target reference is not necessary once the certificate uses the aggregate carrier.  By contrast, if signed increments are admitted while structural-noise variances are required to remain strictly positive, the diagonal covariance \(\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda_e)\) is positive definite if and only if
\[
 \omega_{0,\mu,j}+\lambda_{ej}>0
 \quad\text{for every coordinate }j\text{ and every environment }e. \tag{14}
\]
Indeed, a diagonal symmetric matrix is positive definite exactly when each diagonal entry is positive, because its quadratic form on the \(j\)-th coordinate vector is that entry, and conversely its quadratic form is the sum of positive diagonal entries times squared coordinates.  Equations (5), (7), and (8) show that (14) can hold while the nonnegative-diagonal certificate fails.  This isolates signed shifts as the genuine boundary obstruction and completes the proof.

statements.statement: Fix \(C<\infty\).  For any possibly abstaining rule whose probability of an incorrect classification is uniformly at most \(\alpha\) on \(\Theta_K\), there exists \(\kappa=\kappa(C,\alpha,m,M,d,E)>0\) such that along every sequence \(\theta_n\in\Theta_K\) with \(\delta_n(\theta_n)\le C\), the probability of correctly certifying \(h(\theta_n)\) is at most \(1-\kappa\).
statements.justification: A matching impossibility result makes information distance a genuine certification boundary rather than only a sufficient margin.
statements.gap: Weak-heteroskedasticity tests and repeated-eigenvalue analyses do not construct opposite labeled causal-target strata while preserving acyclicity, stationary confounding, measurement error, range inclusion, and positive noises.
statements.consumer: The bound prevents overconfident effective-target declarations when covariance profiles are statistically indistinguishable.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(C<\infty\), and let \(\theta_n\in\Theta_K\) satisfy \(\delta_n(\theta_n)\le C\).  By the definition of the infimum, choose
\(\zeta_n=(Z_{0n},\ldots,Z_{En})\in\Theta_K\) such that
\[
 h(\zeta_n)\ne h(\theta_n),
 \qquad
 \lVert\zeta_n-\theta_n\rVert_{I,n,\theta_n}<C+1. \tag{35}
\]
This choice does not assume that the opposite-classification set is closed or that the infimum is attained.

We next obtain a uniform likelihood-ratio moment bound.  Put \(R=M/m>1\) and choose \(p>1\) so close to one that
\(p-(p-1)R>0\).  For one observation, with covariance \(\Sigma\) under the denominator law and covariance \(Z\) under the numerator law, let
\(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d\) be the eigenvalues of
\(\Sigma^{-1/2}Z\Sigma^{-1/2}\).  The covariance bounds put them in \([R^{-1},R]\).  Whitening the Gaussian density and evaluating the product of one-dimensional Gaussian integrals gives, for
\(L=dN(0,Z)/dN(0,\Sigma)\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{\Sigma}L^p
 =\prod_{j=1}^d
 \lambda_j^{-(p-1)/2}\{p-(p-1)\lambda_j\}^{-1/2}. \tag{36}
\]
The denominator is positive by the choice of \(p\).  If
\[
 g_p(\lambda)=-\frac{p-1}{2}\log\lambda
 -\frac12\log\{p-(p-1)\lambda\},
\]
then \(g_p(1)=g_p'(1)=0\), and \(g_p''\) is bounded above in absolute value by a finite constant \(K_0=K_0(p,R)\) on \([R^{-1},R]\).  Taylor's theorem therefore gives
\(g_p(\lambda)\le K_0(\lambda-1)^2/2\).

For the independent product samples, multiply (36) over observations and environments.  Since
\[
 \sum_j(\lambda_{ej}-1)^2
 =\operatorname{tr}\!\left[\Sigma_{en}^{-1}(Z_{en}-\Sigma_{en})
          \Sigma_{en}^{-1}(Z_{en}-\Sigma_{en})\right],
\]
equation (35) implies
\[
 \mathbb E_{\theta_n}\left(\frac{dP_{\zeta_n}}{dP_{\theta_n}}\right)^p
 \le \exp\!\left(K_0\lVert\zeta_n-\theta_n\rVert_{I,n,\theta_n}^2\right)
 \le K_C:=\exp\{K_0(C+1)^2\}<\infty. \tag{37}
\]
The constant is independent of \(n\), the allocation, and the selected pair of tuples.

Let \(A_n\) be the event that the possibly abstaining rule reports exactly \(h(\theta_n)\).  Because this classification is wrong under \(\zeta_n\), uniform \(\alpha\)-honesty gives
\(P_{\zeta_n}(A_n)\le\alpha\).  With
\(L_n=dP_{\zeta_n}/dP_{\theta_n}\), H\"older's inequality and (37) give
\[
 1-\alpha
 \le P_{\zeta_n}(A_n^{\mathsf c})
 =\mathbb E_{\theta_n}[L_n\mathbf 1_{A_n^{\mathsf c}}]
 \le K_C^{1/p}P_{\theta_n}(A_n^{\mathsf c})^{(p-1)/p}. \tag{38}
\]
Thus
\[
 P_{\theta_n}(A_n)
 \le1-\kappa,\qquad
 \kappa=(1-\alpha)^{p/(p-1)}K_C^{-1/(p-1)}>0. \tag{39}
\]
Here \(p\) and \(K_C\) depend only on \(C,\alpha,m,M,d,E\) (the displayed bound in fact needs no additional dependence on \(d,E\)).  Equation (39) is the claimed uniform obstruction to correct certification at bounded information distance.

statements.statement: Along the legal path \(\theta_{\gamma}\), \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta_{\gamma})=\{\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{1,4\}\}\) and \(h(\theta_{\gamma})=(\{1\},\{1,2,3,4\})\) for \(\gamma\ne0\), whereas at \(\gamma=0\) all six two-element target sets are compatible and \(h(\theta_0)=(\varnothing,\{1,2,3,4\})\).  If the fixed constants \(m,M\) admit \(\gamma_0>0\) such that \(\theta_{\gamma}\in\Theta_K\) for every \(|\gamma|\le\gamma_0\), then, for equal environment sample sizes, there exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that \(c\sqrt n|\gamma|\le\delta_n(\theta_{\gamma})\le C\sqrt n|\gamma|\) for all sufficiently small nonzero \(\gamma\).
statements.justification: The explicit identity baseline and aggregate carrier preserve the star/all-six collision and compute its first-order information scale.
statements.gap: Rotation-set analyses do not provide a legal acyclic target-family collision with a labeled classification and Gaussian-information rate.
statements.consumer: The example remains a minimal audit case for certificate enumeration, augmentation, and abstention near profile collisions.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(A=[a\ b]\).  The six squared determinants of the two-row submatrices \(A_{\{j,k\},:}\), in pair order \(12,13,14,23,24,34\), are
\[
 1,\ 1,\ 4,\ 1,\ 1,\ 9. \tag{24}
\]
They are all positive.  Along the corrected path,
\[
 \Delta_1=aa^{\mathsf T}+bb^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 \Delta_2=2aa^{\mathsf T}+(2+\gamma)bb^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 \bar Q=3aa^{\mathsf T}+(3+\gamma)bb^{\mathsf T}. \tag{25}
\]
For \(|\gamma|<1\), both aggregate weights are positive, so every two-by-two aggregate principal block is positive definite; its determinant is \(3(3+\gamma)\) times the corresponding number in (24).  Also \(\operatorname{rank}(\bar Q)=2\) and both shift ranges lie in \(\operatorname{span}\{a,b\}=\operatorname{range}(\bar Q)\).  The explicit baseline is \(\Sigma_0=I_4\succ0\).

Consider an ordered pair \(t=(j,k)\).  The unit-lower factor of \(\bar Q_{tt}\) has lower entry \(\ell=\bar Q_{kj}/\bar Q_{jj}\).  The off-diagonal entry obtained by congruently transforming the \(\Delta_1\) block equals
\[
 (\Delta_1)_{kj}-\ell(\Delta_1)_{jj}
 =-\frac{\gamma a_jb_j(a_jb_k-b_ja_k)}{\bar Q_{jj}}. \tag{26}
\]
Equation (26) follows by substituting (25), expanding the numerator
\(\bar Q_{jj}(\Delta_1)_{kj}-\bar Q_{kj}(\Delta_1)_{jj}\), and cancelling the terms with equal weight three.  The row determinants in (24) are nonzero.  Since \(b_1=0\) while \(a_jb_j\ne0\) for \(j=2,3,4\), equation (26) vanishes for \(\gamma\ne0\) exactly when the first pivot is label \(1\).

For the three orders \((1,2),(1,3),(1,4)\), direct elimination gives, respectively,
\[
 \begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
 t&D_t&\Lambda_{1,t}&\Lambda_{2,t}\\ \hline
 (1,2)&\operatorname{diag}(3,3+\gamma)&\operatorname{diag}(1,1)&\operatorname{diag}(2,2+\gamma)\\
 (1,3)&\operatorname{diag}(3,3+\gamma)&\operatorname{diag}(1,1)&\operatorname{diag}(2,2+\gamma)\\
 (1,4)&\operatorname{diag}(3,12+4\gamma)&\operatorname{diag}(1,4)&\operatorname{diag}(2,8+4\gamma).
 \end{array} \tag{27}
\]
All entries are nonnegative for \(|\gamma|<1\).  Thus, when \(\gamma\ne0\), the algebraic fiber is
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta_\gamma)
 =\{\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{1,4\}\}. \tag{28}
\]
At \(\gamma=0\), equation (25) gives \(\Delta_2=2\Delta_1\) and \(\bar Q=3\Delta_1\).  Hence every aggregate \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factor transforms \(\Delta_1\) and \(\Delta_2\) to \(D_t/3\) and \(2D_t/3\), so all six pairs are certified.  The hypotheses of the aggregate sharp-fiber theorem were verified after (25); it converts these algebraic fibers into the asserted causal fibers.  Their intersections and unions give
\(h(\theta_\gamma)=(\{1\},\{1,2,3,4\})\) for \(\gamma\ne0\) and
\(h(\theta_0)=(\varnothing,\{1,2,3,4\})\).  The positive-noise realization theorem, applied for example to \(t=(1,2)\), constructs a legal SCM for each tuple with the displayed baseline \(I_4\); thus legality is proved rather than inserted into the path definition.

It remains to prove the information-distance rate under the stated bounded-class premise.  Let
\[
 D(\zeta,\theta)=\left(\sum_{e=0}^2\lVert Z_e-\Sigma_e\rVert_F^2\right)^{1/2},
 \qquad
 \bar Q(\zeta)=\sum_{e=1}^2(Z_e-Z_0), \tag{29}
\]
and define, for \(j=2,3,4\),
\[
 f_j(\zeta)=\bar Q(\zeta)_{jj}(Z_1-Z_0)_{1j}
 -(Z_1-Z_0)_{jj}\bar Q(\zeta)_{1j}. \tag{30}
\]
Substitution from (25) gives
\[
 f_2(\theta_\gamma)=\gamma,\qquad
 f_3(\theta_\gamma)=2\gamma,\qquad
 f_4(\theta_\gamma)=4\gamma. \tag{31}
\]
At \(\theta_0\), every aggregate two-by-two principal minor is strictly positive.  Choose a bounded neighborhood \(\mathcal U\) of \(\theta_0\) on which they remain positive.  The polynomials in (30) have bounded gradients on the closure of a smaller such neighborhood, so the mean-value theorem supplies \(K<\infty\) such that
\[
 \max_{j=2,3,4}|f_j(\zeta)-f_j(\theta_\gamma)|
 \le K D(\zeta,\theta_\gamma) \tag{32}
\]
whenever both tuples lie in that neighborhood.

If \(\zeta\in\Theta_K\cap\mathcal U\) and
\(D(\zeta,\theta_\gamma)<|\gamma|/(2K)\), then (31)--(32) make all three \(f_j(\zeta)\) nonzero.  The initial pivot proportionality equation for first pivot \(j\) would force \(f_j(\zeta)=0\) by taking row \(1\).  Hence no certificate starts at \(2,3,4\).  Membership in \(\Theta_K\) guarantees that a certificate exists, so it starts at \(1\).  After that pivot the aggregate residual has rank one.  Every remaining aggregate residual diagonal is positive because the corresponding two-by-two principal minor stays positive.  Range reconstruction from the existing certificate writes each full shift as a nonnegative sum of its certified columns; after eliminating label \(1\), each shift residual is therefore positive semidefinite and has range in the rank-one aggregate residual range.  It is a nonnegative scalar multiple of that aggregate residual.  Consequently every remaining label is an admissible second pivot, and the fiber is exactly the star in (28).

Choose \(\mathcal U\) to contain a fixed ball about \(\theta_0\).  Since \(\theta_\gamma\to\theta_0\), points outside \(\mathcal U\) have a fixed positive \(D\)-distance from \(\theta_\gamma\) for all sufficiently small \(|\gamma|\).  Combining this with the preceding paragraph yields \(c_0>0\) such that every \(\zeta\in\Theta_K\) with \(h(\zeta)\ne h(\theta_\gamma)\) satisfies
\[
 D(\zeta,\theta_\gamma)\ge c_0|\gamma|. \tag{33}
\]

For equal environment sample sizes \(n\), the covariance bounds imply, for every displacement \(H\),
\[
 \frac{\sqrt n}{\sqrt2M}\left(\sum_{e=0}^2\lVert H_e\rVert_F^2\right)^{1/2}
 \le\lVert H\rVert_{I,n,\theta_\gamma}
 \le\frac{\sqrt n}{\sqrt2m}\left(\sum_{e=0}^2\lVert H_e\rVert_F^2\right)^{1/2}. \tag{34}
\]
Indeed, write \(K_e=\Sigma_e^{-1/2}H_e\Sigma_e^{-1/2}\), use
\(\lVert H_e\rVert_F\le M\lVert K_e\rVert_F\) and
\(\lVert K_e\rVert_F\le m^{-1}\lVert H_e\rVert_F\), and sum the defining quadratic forms.  The left inequality in (34) and (33) give
\[
 \delta_n(\theta_\gamma)\ge\frac{c_0}{\sqrt2M}\sqrt n\,|\gamma|. \tag{35}
\]
For the reverse inequality, the premise places \(\theta_0\) in \(\Theta_K\), and its classification differs from that of every nonzero \(\gamma\).  Only environment \(2\) changes, by \(\gamma bb^{\mathsf T}\).  Hence the right inequality in (34) gives
\[
 \delta_n(\theta_\gamma)
 \le\lVert\theta_0-\theta_\gamma\rVert_{I,n,\theta_\gamma}
 \le\frac{\sqrt n}{\sqrt2m}|\gamma|\lVert bb^{\mathsf T}\rVert_F. \tag{36}
\]
Equations (35)--(36) prove the asserted constants \(0<c<C<\infty\).

statements.statement: When \(r=1\) and \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\ne\varnothing\), the sharp fiber reduces to \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)=\{\{j\}:Q_{jj}>0\}\).
statements.justification: This reduction checks that the multivariate certificate collapses to the known rank-one changing-column ambiguity.
statements.gap: The rank-one case is implicit in covariance-factor arguments, but is stated here as the required sanity reduction of the general labeled-fiber theorem.
statements.consumer: Practitioners with single effective perturbations obtain a closed-form candidate list without running the recursion.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume \(r=1\) and \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\ne\varnothing\).  The sharp-fiber theorem gives a certified singleton \(\{k\}\).  Its realization, or equivalently range reconstruction applied to its certificate, shows that
\(Q=aa^{\mathsf T}d\) for some \(d>0\); hence \(Q\) is positive semidefinite of rank one.  For every \(e\), symmetry and
\(\operatorname{range}(\Delta_e)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Q)=\operatorname{span}\{a\}\) imply
\(\Delta_e=c_eQ\) for a scalar \(c_e\).  At the certified coordinate \(k\), the scalar certificate equals
\(\Delta_{e,kk}/Q_{kk}=c_e\), so nonnegativity of that certificate gives \(c_e\ge0\).

Now fix any label \(j\).  For the one-element order \(t=(j)\), the reference block is the scalar \(Q_{jj}\).  It is positive exactly when \(Q_{jj}>0\); in that case its unit-lower factor is \(L_t=(1)\), and every transformed block is the scalar
\[
 \Lambda_{e,t}=\Delta_{e,jj}=c_eQ_{jj}\ge0.
\]
Thus \(\{j\}\) is certified exactly when \(Q_{jj}>0\).  Applying the sharp-fiber equality proves
\(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)=\{\{j\}:Q_{jj}>0\}\).

statements.statement:
There is no universal correct-certification envelope determined only by \(c=\lim\delta_n(\theta_n)\).  For any specified Gaussian tangent geometry \(\mathcal G=(k,g_0,\mathcal A)\), where \(X\sim N(g,I_k)\), \(g_0\) has the focal classification, and \(\mathcal A\) is the opposite-classification tangent set, the geometry-indexed focal-certification value is
\[
 \beta^{\star}_{\mathcal G}(\alpha)
 =\sup_{\substack{\phi:\mathbb R^k\to[0,1]\ \mathrm{Borel}\\
                    \sup_{g\in\mathcal A}\mathbb E_g\phi(X)\le\alpha}}
   \mathbb E_{g_0}\phi(X).
\]
The nearest-opposite distance \(c=\inf_{g\in\mathcal A}\lVert g-g_0\rVert_2\) does not determine this value.  Explicitly, for \(k=1\), \(g_0=0\), and opposite sets \(\mathcal A_+=[c,\infty)\) and \(\mathcal A_{\pm}=(-\infty,-c]\cup[c,\infty)\), with \(c>0\),
\[
 \beta^{\star}_{\mathcal G_+}(\alpha)=\Phi(\Phi^{-1}(\alpha)+c),
 \qquad
 \beta^{\star}_{\mathcal G_{\pm}}(\alpha)=2\Phi(t_{c,\alpha})-1
 <\beta^{\star}_{\mathcal G_+}(\alpha),
\]
where \(\Phi\) is the standard-normal distribution function and \(t_{c,\alpha}>0\) is the unique solution of \(\Phi(t-c)-\Phi(-t-c)=\alpha\).  Thus the handle yields an explicit optimization only after the incident tangent geometry is supplied; neither a one-variable \(\beta^{\star}(c)\) nor one classifier attaining it uniformly over all regular sequences is determined by the frozen core.
statements.proof_tex:
The displayed optimization follows directly from the meaning of an \(\alpha\)-honest focal-class certificate in the Gaussian shift experiment.  A randomized certificate is a Borel function \(\phi\) taking values in \([0,1]\).  At the focal shift its correct-certification probability is \(\mathbb E_{g_0}\phi(X)\), while at an opposite-classification shift \(g\) the same report is incorrect, so honesty imposes \(\mathbb E_g\phi(X)\le\alpha\).  Conversely, any such \(\phi\) extends to a possibly abstaining complete classifier by assigning probability \(\phi(X)\) to the focal report, zero to every nonfocal report, and the remaining probability to abstention.  Thus no additional action can increase the probability of the correct focal report, and taking the supremum gives the stated geometry-indexed value.  This step distinguishes the causal classification from its limiting decision functional: the optimization is obtained only after the tangent experiment and its classification strata have been derived.

We now calculate two geometries having the same nearest-opposite distance.  Let \(p_u\) be the density of \(N(u,1)\), and first take \(\mathcal A_+=[c,\infty)\).  The likelihood ratio at its nearest point is
\[
 \frac{p_0(x)}{p_c(x)}=\exp\{-cx+c^2/2\} \tag{37}
\]
is strictly decreasing in \(x\).  Put \(a=c+\Phi^{-1}(\alpha)\) and \(A=(-\infty,a]\), so \(P_c(A)=\alpha\).  To prove optimality without invoking an undeclared testing theorem, set \(K=p_0(a)/p_c(a)\).  For any measurable \(0\le\phi\le1\) with \(E_c\phi\le\alpha\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_0\phi-P_0(A)
 &=\int(\phi-\mathbf1_A)\frac{p_0}{p_c}\,dP_c\\
 &=\int(\phi-\mathbf1_A)\left(\frac{p_0}{p_c}-K\right)dP_c
   +K\{E_c\phi-P_c(A)\}\le0. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{38}
\]
On \(A\), the first factor \(\phi-1\) is nonpositive and the likelihood-ratio difference is nonnegative; off \(A\), the two signs are reversed.  The last term is nonpositive by feasibility.  Moreover, for every \(u\ge c\),
\(P_u(A)=\Phi(a-u)\le\Phi(a-c)=\alpha\), so \(\mathbf1_A\) is feasible for the entire opposite set.  Since every rule feasible for the entire set is feasible at \(u=c\), inequality (38) proves optimality and
\[
 \beta^{\star}_{\mathcal G_+}(\alpha)=P_0(A)
 =\Phi(c+\Phi^{-1}(\alpha)). \tag{39}
\]
Strict monotonicity in (37) also shows that this optimizer is unique up to null sets.

Now take \(\mathcal A_{\pm}=(-\infty,-c]\cup[c,\infty)\).  Given any feasible \(\phi\), symmetrize it as
\(\psi(x)=\{\phi(x)+\phi(-x)\}/2\).  Then \(E_0\psi=E_0\phi\), and
\[
 E_c\psi=E_{-c}\psi=\frac{E_c\phi+E_{-c}\phi}{2}\le\alpha. \tag{40}
\]
Let \(Q=(P_c+P_{-c})/2\).  Its density satisfies
\[
 \frac{p_0(x)}{dQ/dx}
 =\frac{e^{c^2/2}}{\cosh(cx)}, \tag{41}
\]
which is strictly decreasing in \(|x|\).  The function
\(t\mapsto Q([-t,t])=\Phi(t-c)-\Phi(-t-c)\) is continuous and strictly increasing from zero to one.  Hence there is a unique \(t_{c,\alpha}>0\) for which this probability equals \(\alpha\).

Apply the same signed-integrand calculation as in (38), now with the density ratio in (41), the measure \(Q\), and the central interval \(A_{\pm}=[-t_{c,\alpha},t_{c,\alpha}]\).  It proves that every \(\psi\) with \(E_Q\psi\le\alpha\) satisfies
\(E_0\psi\le P_0(A_{\pm})\).  The indicator of \(A_{\pm}\) has probability \(\alpha\) under both \(P_c\) and \(P_{-c}\).  For \(u\ge0\),
\[
 \frac{d}{du}P_u(A_{\pm})
 =-\varphi(t_{c,\alpha}-u)+\varphi(t_{c,\alpha}+u)\le0, \tag{42}
\]
where \(\varphi\) is the standard-normal density; the inequality follows because
\(|t_{c,\alpha}+u|\ge|t_{c,\alpha}-u|\).  Symmetry gives the same monotonicity in \(|u|\), so the indicator is feasible for every \(|u|\ge c\).  Therefore
\[
 \beta^{\star}_{\mathcal G_{\pm}}(\alpha)
 =P_0(A_{\pm})=2\Phi(t_{c,\alpha})-1. \tag{43}
\]

The feasible set for \(\mathcal G_{\pm}\) is contained in that for \(\mathcal G_+\).  Equality of the two optima would force the unique one-sided optimizer \(\mathbf1_{(-\infty,a]}\) from (39) to satisfy the additional constraint under \(P_{-c}\).  It does not, because
\[
 P_{-c}(( -\infty,a])=\Phi(a+c)
 =\Phi(\Phi^{-1}(\alpha)+2c)>\alpha. \tag{44}
\]
Thus the inequality in the theorem is strict.  Both geometries have nearest-opposite Euclidean distance \(c\), yet their exact optimal honest certification probabilities differ.  The corrected handle records its Gaussian tangent experiment in information-whitened coordinates, so its Euclidean distance is, by construction, the limiting information distance.  Thus \(\lim\delta_n=c\) retains the nearest distance but not the number or arrangement of incident opposite-classification regions.  The scalar cannot determine a universal envelope or a common attaining rule.  Supplying \(\mathcal G\), as in the corrected handle, is necessary and gives the explicit computable optimization stated above.
statements.justification: The scalar information distance is only a nearest-boundary summary; honest local certification must be indexed by the complete incident tangent geometry.
statements.gap: Weak-identification theory does not provide a universal one-variable power envelope for a finite causal classification with different incident semialgebraic cone geometries.
statements.consumer: An analyst can compute a local certification benchmark after deriving the tangent geometry of the particular collision, while avoiding unsupported universal calibration by the scalar distance alone.
